request.spec:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.

agent.result_text:
Watching people is in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass on the first run.

**What a user sees:** each person's row has a new **Watched** cell showing `yes`/`no` for whoever is signed in, plus a Watch/Unwatch button (`person-watch`). If the toggle is refused, the row's usual `person-error` message appears. Taking any other action on that row clears it, the same way it works for hold and retire.

**Stored data:** a new `person_watch` table (migration `V39__person_watch.sql`) holds one row per watching user. Stopping deletes the row. Starting again adds a new row, so that user moves to the end of the "order they started watching".

**Server:**
- `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/watch` turns the watch on or off for that user and writes `PERSON_WATCHED` or `PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>`. A request without a user is refused.
- `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/watches?user=<name>` returns the ids of the people that user watches. The front end uses it to show yes/no.
- The `NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name> number=<number>` lines come from `Watches.notify`. It runs straight after the claim's own audit line and before the rollup lines:
  - in `RecordClaimStatusChanged`, only when a settle actually settles or an approve goes through
  - in `RecordClaimResettled`, on every re-settle

**Things you might not expect:**
- **Bulk settle also notifies.** It reuses the single-settle audit step, so each settled claim gets its own NOTIFY lines; one of the tests expects this.
- **A clerk's settle over the limit doesn't notify.** The claim only goes PENDING, which isn't a settle.
- **Bulk open had to change too.** `OpenClaims.java` reuses the same audit step, so I updated its call to match the new signature. Opening a claim never writes NOTIFY lines.

The front end is a new `features/watch/watch.slot.tsx` that adds itself to the row.
